existing_trusted_path.execution: Run inside the authorized aidream trusted consumer, with exact connection_id, acting user_id, organization_id and audited credential purpose. Keep the derived token in process and send it only to the official Google endpoint.
existing_trusted_path.scope_admission: Use required_scope_options for either chromewebstore.readonly or chromewebstore when reading status. Declare scope strings in the canonical Google scope registries before a real consumer is implemented; do not add consent implicitly.
existing_trusted_path.not_an_agent_token_route: The existing /api/google-integrations/internal/credential bridge returns credential material to authorized server consumers. It is not a route for exposing a sealed Google credential to an agent or shell. Browser /api/vault/resolve excludes sealed values.

prepared_activation_sequence: First restore or expose the supported trusted-server connector/invocation and inspect only metadata for the exact publisher Google connection, including provider account identity and granted scopes. Confirm Chrome Web Store API is enabled in the existing ai-matrix-engine Google Cloud project. No token value is needed in chat, shell arguments, logs or repository secrets.

Obtain the non-secret API publisher ID from the official Developer Dashboard Publisher > Settings for Matrx through permitted account access. Do not guess it from the publisher display name, extension ID or public listing. The current Browser Use refusal is a tool constraint; do not route around it.

If the exact publisher connection already holds an accepted Store scope, implement an in-process read-only Store consumer using the canonical resolver. If no accepted grant exists, prepare an explicit official OAuth consent flow for the chosen Store operation, preserving every existing Google grant. For status alone request chromewebstore.readonly; upload/publish require chromewebstore. A new grant is not inferred from the existing Google login.

An official server-to-server alternative is a Google Cloud service account linked under the Store Developer Dashboard Account section. Google permits one linked service account per publisher. Check existing linkage before changing it; do not replace one silently. Prefer supported short-lived token issuance through the trusted server. Creating a service account alone does not grant Store authority; this linkage remains unverified and was not performed.

Before any mutation, issue GET https://chromewebstore.googleapis.com/v2/publishers/{verifiedPublisherId}/items/hnfolienncfklkgmdjjmhhegglimlamg:fetchStatus with an empty body. Require response name and itemId to match exactly; retain only timestamp, identity and review/version fields. Read publishedItemRevisionStatus and submittedItemRevisionStatus separately, including distributionChannels[].crxVersion, state, takenDown, warned and lastAsyncUploadState. A successful token refresh alone earns no Store access or status credit.

After read-only identity/status verification, independently review and test the real consumer before enabling any upload/publish step. Keep it separate from package generation. Reconcile the exact guarded hosted ZIP, provenance and digest; refuse to replace a pending submission merely because main advanced. Upload uses POST /upload/v2/publishers/{publisherId}/items/{itemId}:upload. Submit uses POST /v2/publishers/{publisherId}/items/{itemId}:publish with DEFAULT_PUBLISH and skipReview false. Verify returned state and a fresh fetchStatus; do not silently retry an uncertain mutation. Existing listing/privacy reconciliation and package gates still apply.
